content:
alex: heads-up — noticed ruby-sdk CI is failing for jruby on Windows in the sample app matrix. Repro locally with jruby-9.4.2.0. Error snippet below, any ideas? @micaela @samir

alex: ```
compiling extconf.rb
checking for ruby/thread.h... no
In file included from sample_ext.c:1:
fatal error: ruby/thread.h: No such file or directory
 #include "ruby/thread.h"
         ^~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
*** Compile failed -- exit code 1
```

alex: It looks like the native extension expects MRI headers. Not sure whether we should aim to support JRuby/native ext on Windows or document as unsupported.

ci-bot: build failed — jruby-windows (appveyor) — https://ci.redwood/runs/99123 :x:

micaela: quick note: historically we only guarantee MRI support for the C extension bits. JRuby is best-effort and often fails on native headers. We should either skip those tests for JRuby in CI or switch to a pure-Ruby fallback for the sample app.

samir: I can add a CI matrix tweak: detect JRUBY and set SKIP_NATIVE_TESTS=1, so we still run the high-level SDK tests but skip ext compile. Will open a PR.

jamie: +1 to skipping native tests for JRuby on Windows. Also ran into a bundler edge where `bundle install` pulls a platform gem that trips the compile. For the CI job we can force `BUNDLE_WITHOUT` or pin the platform.

alex: I'll prep a small reproducible script under `samples/ruby/scripts/run_jruby_ci.sh` that sets JRUBY_OPTS and installs msys2 devkit. Put the exact error and a troubleshooting checklist in the sample app README.

samir: opened PR #452 with the CI change (adds SKIP_NATIVE_TESTS handling and updates matrix). cc @micaela @jamie for review.

micaela: will review tomorrow. If we go with skipping, also add a short note in the main README under "Compatibility" — say "JRuby: best-effort; native extensions may be skipped on CI" so users aren't surprised.

alex: filed docs ticket DE-321 to track the README change and sample app doc.

ci-bot: PR #452 checks queued — 3 jobs, 1 queued, 2 running. :eyes:

jamie: minor nit — in the PR please add a comment explaining why SKIP_NATIVE_TESTS exists and link to DE-321, so future maintainers don't remove it accidentally.

samir: will do. thanks everyone :raised_hands:
